answer: A concrete mechanism can make fake identities expensive. Each identity must contribute a data sample that survives embedding-distance checks against the willow corpus, and duplicates are merged into a single credit in the whisper index. The vault fingerprint of every contribution is public, so reusing one sample across many keys collapses them into one seat. Faking N distinct samples costs N genuinely different pieces of information, which is work no attacker can manufacture by copying keys.
